events.title: First settlers reach Ireland
events.description: Mesolithic hunter-gatherers cross from Britain after the ice retreats. The camp at Mount Sandel on the River Bann is among the oldest known settlements in Ireland.

events.title: Neolithic farming begins
events.description: Farmers arrive with cattle, cereals and polished stone tools. At Ceide Fields in Mayo they lay out stone field walls later buried under bog - among the oldest known field systems in the world.

events.title: Newgrange passage tomb built
events.description: The great passage tomb in the Boyne Valley is constructed, older than Stonehenge and the pyramids. Its roof-box is aligned so the rising sun floods the chamber at the winter solstice.

events.title: Megalithic cemeteries at Carrowmore
events.description: Clusters of passage tombs and dolmens are raised across the west, marking territory and ancestry for the farming communities.

events.title: Bronze Age and copper mining
events.description: Copper is mined at Ross Island in Kerry and alloyed with tin into bronze. Irish gold ornaments from this period are traded across Britain and the Continent.

events.title: Iron Age and Celtic culture
events.description: Iron working, La Tene art styles and the Celtic languages take hold. Ireland is divided among many small kingdoms (tuatha) under regional overkings.

events.title: Tara emerges as a royal centre
events.description: The Hill of Tara becomes the ceremonial seat of the kings of Mide and later the symbolic seat of the High Kingship of Ireland.

events.title: Ptolemy maps Ireland
events.description: The Alexandrian geographer Ptolemy records the coasts, rivers and peoples of the island he calls Ivernia - the first written description of Ireland.

events.title: Irish raids on Roman Britain
events.description: Irish raiders attack the western coasts of a weakening Roman Britain, taking slaves. Tradition holds that one such captive was the young Patrick.

events.title: Palladius sent to the Irish
events.description: Pope Celestine sends Palladius as first bishop 'to the Irish believing in Christ' - proof that Christian communities already existed on the island.

events.title: Patrick's mission begins
events.description: By tradition Patrick returns to Ireland as a missionary bishop, having earlier been held there as a slave. His church at Armagh becomes the primatial see.

events.title: Clonmacnoise founded
events.description: Ciaran founds a monastery at a crossing of the Shannon. It grows into a major centre of learning, craftwork and burial for the kings of Connacht and Tara.

events.title: Derry founded by Colmcille
events.description: Colmcille (Columba) establishes a monastery in an oak grove - Doire - that gives Derry its name.

events.title: Colmcille founds Iona
events.description: Exiled to Scotland, Colmcille founds Iona, launching the Irish mission that will convert much of northern Britain and reach deep into Europe.

events.title: Glendalough founded
events.description: Kevin establishes a hermitage in a glacial valley in Wicklow that becomes one of Ireland's great monastic cities and pilgrimage sites.

events.title: Columbanus sails for the Continent
events.description: Columbanus leaves for Gaul and founds monasteries at Luxeuil and Bobbio, spreading Irish learning and penitential practice across Europe.

events.title: Synod of Whitby and plague
events.description: The Roman dating of Easter prevails over the Irish at Whitby, while a severe plague sweeps Ireland, killing kings and abbots alike.

events.title: Cain Adomnain, the Law of Innocents
events.description: Adomnan of Iona promulgates a law protecting women, children and clerics from violence in war - an early codified protection of non-combatants.

events.title: Golden age of manuscript art
events.description: Irish scriptoria produce illuminated gospel books such as the Book of Durrow, fusing Celtic ornament with Mediterranean and Germanic motifs.

events.title: The Book of Kells
events.description: The most lavish of the Insular gospel books is created, probably begun on Iona and completed at Kells. It survives today in Trinity College Dublin.

events.title: First Viking raid
events.description: Norse raiders sack the island monastery of Rathlin off the Antrim coast, beginning two centuries of attack, trade and settlement.

events.title: Monks flee Iona for Kells
events.description: After repeated massacres on Iona, the Columban community relocates its treasures and scholarship to Kells in Meath.

events.title: Dublin founded as a longphort
events.description: Vikings establish a fortified ship harbour on the Liffey. The Norse town of Dyflin becomes a major slave and silver market of the northern world.

events.title: Waterford established
events.description: A second wave of Norse settlement founds Waterford, followed by Wexford, Cork and Limerick - Ireland's first true towns.

events.title: Brian Boru takes Munster
events.description: Brian mac Cennetig succeeds his brother and begins the campaign that will make him the most powerful king in Ireland, ruling from Cashel.

events.title: Brian Boru claims the High Kingship
events.description: Brian Boru forces the submission of the northern kings and is recognised as High King, briefly uniting Ireland under one ruler.

events.title: Battle of Clontarf
events.description: Brian Boru's forces defeat a Leinster-Norse alliance outside Dublin, but Brian is killed in his tent. The High Kingship fragments again.

events.title: Synod of Rath Breasail
events.description: The Irish church is reorganised on a diocesan and territorial basis, reducing the power of the great monastic federations.

events.title: First Cistercian abbey at Mellifont
events.description: Malachy of Armagh brings the Cistercians to Ireland, importing continental monastic architecture and discipline.

events.title: Diarmait Mac Murchada driven out
events.description: The King of Leinster is expelled by his rivals and sails to seek help from Henry II - the invitation that brings the Normans to Ireland.

events.title: Normans land at Bannow Bay
events.description: The first Cambro-Norman force lands in Wexford in Mac Murchada's service, bringing mailed cavalry, archers and castle-building to Ireland.

events.title: Strongbow takes Waterford and Dublin
events.description: Richard de Clare, 'Strongbow', storms Waterford, marries Mac Murchada's daughter Aoife, and seizes Dublin - making himself heir to Leinster.

events.title: Henry II lands in Ireland
events.description: Alarmed by Strongbow's independence, Henry II arrives with a royal army. Irish and Norman lords submit, and the Lordship of Ireland is created under the English crown.

events.title: De Courcy invades Ulster
events.description: John de Courcy carves out a private lordship in the north-east, building castles at Carrickfergus and Dundrum.

events.title: Dublin Castle begun
events.description: King John orders a castle at Dublin to hold his treasure and administer the lordship. It remains the seat of English power in Ireland for seven centuries.

events.title: Conquest of Connacht
events.description: Norman lords complete the invasion of the west, and the settlement reaches its greatest extent across roughly three-quarters of the island.

events.title: First representative parliament
events.description: A parliament meets in Dublin with elected county representatives, extending English legal and administrative structures across the colony.

events.title: Edward Bruce invades
events.description: The brother of Robert the Bruce lands in Ulster and is crowned King of Ireland. Three years of war and famine devastate the country before his defeat in 1318.

events.title: The Black Death reaches Ireland
events.description: Plague arrives at the ports and cuts hardest through the crowded Anglo-Irish towns, weakening the colony relative to the rural Gaelic lordships.

events.title: Statutes of Kilkenny
events.description: Parliament bans the settlers from speaking Irish, marrying the Irish or following Brehon law - an admission that the colony was assimilating rather than conquering.

events.title: Richard II's expedition
events.description: Richard II lands with the largest English army yet sent to Ireland and receives the submission of the Gaelic kings, though the settlement does not hold.

events.title: Gaelic resurgence and the Pale
events.description: Gaelic and gaelicised lords recover most of the island. English authority contracts to a fortified enclave around Dublin known as the Pale.

events.title: Poynings' Law
events.description: The Irish parliament is subordinated to the English crown and council, unable to meet or legislate without prior approval. It stands until 1782.

events.title: Silken Thomas rebels
events.description: Thomas FitzGerald renounces allegiance to Henry VIII. The rising is crushed and the Kildare Geraldines, long the real rulers of the lordship, are destroyed.

events.title: The Reformation reaches Ireland
events.description: The Irish Reformation Parliament makes Henry VIII head of the church in Ireland and begins dissolving the monasteries. Most of the population remains Catholic - the fault line of the next four centuries.

events.title: Henry VIII declared King of Ireland
events.description: The lordship becomes a kingdom, and a policy of 'surrender and regrant' begins converting Gaelic chiefs into crown tenants holding English titles.

events.title: First plantations in Laois and Offaly
events.description: Crown land is confiscated and settled with English colonists in the midlands, establishing the template for later, larger plantations.

events.title: Second Desmond Rebellion
events.description: Munster rises under the Earl of Desmond. The war is fought with scorched earth and ends in a famine that empties much of the province.

events.title: Spanish Armada wrecks on the coast
events.description: More than twenty Armada ships are driven onto the western and northern shores. Thousands drown or are killed on landing.

events.title: The Nine Years War begins
events.description: Hugh O'Neill of Tyrone and Hugh O'Donnell lead the most serious Gaelic challenge to Tudor rule, fielding armies trained and equipped on the European model.

events.title: Battle of the Yellow Ford
events.description: O'Neill destroys an English army near Armagh in the worst defeat suffered by the crown in Ireland, and the rebellion spreads nationwide.

events.title: Battle of Kinsale
events.description: A Spanish force lands at Kinsale in the far south. O'Neill and O'Donnell march the length of Ireland to join it and are routed - the decisive defeat of Gaelic Ireland.

events.title: Flight of the Earls
events.description: O'Neill, O'Donnell and their followers sail from Rathmullan for the Continent, abandoning their lands. It marks the end of the old Gaelic aristocratic order.

events.title: Plantation of Ulster
events.description: Six escheated counties are granted to English and Scottish Protestant settlers. The most thorough of the plantations, it reshapes the population and politics of the north permanently.

events.title: The Irish Rebellion
events.description: Dispossessed Catholic gentry rise in Ulster. The killings of settlers, and the vastly inflated accounts of them, harden English opinion for a generation.

events.title: Confederation of Kilkenny
events.description: Catholic Ireland forms its own governing assembly at Kilkenny, ruling much of the country for most of the following decade.

events.title: Cromwell storms Drogheda
events.description: Cromwell lands with the New Model Army and takes Drogheda, putting the garrison to the sword; Wexford follows. The campaign breaks organised resistance.

events.title: Cromwellian settlement
events.description: The Act for the Settlement of Ireland confiscates Catholic land wholesale and transplants owners west of the Shannon. Catholic landholding collapses from around 60 per cent to under 10.

events.title: Battle of the Boyne
events.description: William of Orange defeats the deposed James II on the Boyne near Drogheda. The battle becomes the founding memory of Irish Protestant identity.

events.title: Aughrim and the Treaty of Limerick
events.description: The Jacobite army is destroyed at Aughrim, the bloodiest battle ever fought in Ireland. Limerick surrenders on terms, and the defeated soldiers sail for France as the 'Wild Geese'.

events.title: The Penal Laws begin
events.description: A series of statutes strips Catholics of the right to bear arms, be educated, buy land, hold office or inherit intact estates. Presbyterians face lesser disabilities.

events.title: Test Act extends the restrictions
events.description: Office holders must take communion in the established church, excluding Catholics and Presbyterians alike from public life.

events.title: Catholics lose the vote
events.description: The remaining Catholic franchise is abolished, completing the legal architecture of the Protestant Ascendancy.

events.title: The Year of the Slaughter
events.description: An extreme freeze followed by drought destroys the harvest. Bliain an Air kills perhaps a fifth of the population - proportionally worse than the Great Famine a century later.

events.title: Grattan's Parliament
events.description: With Britain distracted by the American war and the Volunteers under arms, Poynings' Law is repealed and the Irish parliament wins legislative independence.

events.title: United Irishmen founded
events.description: Inspired by the American and French revolutions, Wolfe Tone and others found the Society of United Irishmen in Belfast, seeking to unite Catholic, Protestant and Dissenter.

events.title: Orange Order founded
events.description: After sectarian fighting at the Diamond near Loughgall, the Orange Order is formed to defend the Protestant interest.

events.title: French fleet at Bantry Bay
events.description: A French invasion fleet carrying Wolfe Tone reaches Bantry Bay but is scattered by storms and never lands.

events.title: The United Irish Rebellion
events.description: Risings break out in Wexford, Antrim, Down and Mayo. The rebels are broken at Vinegar Hill and perhaps 30,000 die in a few months of savage fighting.

events.title: Act of Union
events.description: The Irish parliament votes itself out of existence. From 1 January 1801 Ireland is governed directly from Westminster as part of the United Kingdom.

events.title: Emmet's rising
events.description: Robert Emmet's attempted insurrection in Dublin fails within hours. His speech from the dock becomes a foundational nationalist text.

events.title: The Catholic Association
events.description: Daniel O'Connell founds a mass political movement funded by a penny-a-month 'Catholic rent', mobilising the rural poor as a political force.

events.title: Catholic Emancipation
events.description: After O'Connell wins Clare and cannot legally take his seat, Westminster concedes the right of Catholics to sit in parliament and hold most offices.

events.title: National school system established
events.description: A state primary system is created, spreading literacy in English rapidly and accelerating the decline of the Irish language.

events.title: Monster meeting at Tara
events.description: Perhaps three-quarters of a million people gather at Tara to hear O'Connell demand repeal of the Union. The government bans the next meeting and the campaign stalls.

events.title: Potato blight arrives
events.description: Phytophthora infestans destroys the crop on which roughly a third of the population depends entirely for food.

events.title: Black '47
events.description: The worst year of the Great Famine. Relief is inadequate and ideologically constrained while food continues to be exported. Mass death from starvation and fever.

events.title: Young Ireland rising
events.description: A brief and easily suppressed rebellion in Tipperary, but its separatist writings shape later republicanism.

events.title: The Famine ends
events.description: By its close roughly one million have died and another million emigrated. The population falls from about 8.5 million to 6.5 million and keeps falling for eighty years.

events.title: The Fenians founded
events.description: The Irish Republican Brotherhood is founded in Dublin and the Fenian Brotherhood in New York, establishing the transatlantic pattern of Irish republican organisation.

events.title: Fenian Rising
events.description: A poorly coordinated rising fails, but Fenian actions in Britain push Irish grievances to the centre of British politics.

events.title: The Land War begins
events.description: Michael Davitt founds the Land League with Parnell as president. Rent strikes, boycotts and agitation force a series of acts that transfer ownership to tenant farmers.

events.title: GAA founded
events.description: The Gaelic Athletic Association is founded in Thurles to revive hurling and Gaelic football, becoming a mass cultural and nationalist institution.

events.title: First Home Rule Bill
events.description: Gladstone's bill for an Irish parliament splits the Liberal Party and is defeated. Ulster unionism mobilises in opposition.

events.title: Parnell falls and dies
events.description: The divorce scandal splits the Irish Parliamentary Party and Parnell dies months later at 45, leaving constitutional nationalism divided for a decade.

events.title: Gaelic League founded
events.description: Douglas Hyde and Eoin MacNeill found Conradh na Gaeilge to revive the Irish language, seeding a cultural nationalism that radicalises a generation.

events.title: Sinn Fein founded
events.description: Arthur Griffith launches a party advocating Irish self-reliance and abstention from Westminster.

events.title: Ulster Covenant and Home Rule crisis
events.description: Nearly half a million sign the Ulster Covenant against Home Rule. Both unionist and nationalist volunteer militias arm, bringing Ireland to the edge of civil war.

events.title: The Dublin Lockout
events.description: Twenty thousand workers under James Larkin are locked out for months in a bitter industrial dispute. The Irish Citizen Army is formed out of it.

events.title: Home Rule passed and suspended
events.description: Home Rule finally reaches the statute book but is suspended for the duration of the First World War. Some 200,000 Irishmen serve in the British forces.

events.title: The Easter Rising
events.description: Republicans seize the General Post Office and other buildings in Dublin and proclaim a republic. The rising is crushed in a week, but the execution of sixteen leaders transforms public opinion.

events.title: Sinn Fein landslide
events.description: Sinn Fein wins 73 of 105 Irish seats on a platform of abstention and an independent republic, displacing the Irish Parliamentary Party.

events.title: First Dail and War of Independence
events.description: The elected members convene their own parliament in Dublin and declare independence. On the same day the first shots of the guerrilla war are fired at Soloheadbeg.

events.title: Bloody Sunday
events.description: IRA units kill British intelligence officers in the morning; that afternoon crown forces fire into the crowd at a football match in Croke Park, killing fourteen.

events.title: Government of Ireland Act partitions Ireland
events.description: The island is divided into Northern Ireland and Southern Ireland, each with its own parliament. Only the northern one functions as intended.

events.title: Anglo-Irish Treaty
events.description: The Treaty creates the Irish Free State as a dominion, with an oath to the crown and the option for Northern Ireland to opt out, which it immediately does.

events.title: Civil War and the death of Collins
events.description: Pro- and anti-Treaty forces go to war. Michael Collins is killed in an ambush at Beal na Blath in his native Cork.

events.title: Civil War ends
events.description: The anti-Treaty side dumps arms. The war leaves lasting bitterness and defines the two main parties of Irish politics for the next century.

events.title: Fianna Fail founded
events.description: De Valera leaves Sinn Fein to found a party that will enter the Dail, bringing the anti-Treaty side into constitutional politics.

events.title: De Valera takes power
events.description: Fianna Fail wins office and the outgoing government hands over peacefully - a decisive moment for the young democracy. The Economic War with Britain follows.

events.title: Bunreacht na hEireann
events.description: A new constitution replaces the Free State, creates the office of President, claims jurisdiction over the whole island and gives the Catholic Church a 'special position'.

events.title: The Emergency and neutrality
events.description: Ireland stays neutral through the Second World War, a policy that asserts sovereignty but leaves the state isolated and short of supplies.

events.title: The Belfast Blitz
events.description: German raids on Belfast kill around 1,000 people. Fire crews cross the border from the neutral south to help.

events.title: The Republic declared
events.description: Ireland formally leaves the Commonwealth and becomes a republic. Westminster responds by guaranteeing Northern Ireland's position within the UK.

events.title: Ireland joins the United Nations
events.description: Admitted after a decade of Cold War deadlock, Ireland begins a long tradition of UN peacekeeping.

events.title: Lemass and the opening of the economy
events.description: Sean Lemass succeeds de Valera and, with T.K. Whitaker, replaces protectionism with free trade and foreign investment. Emigration slows and living standards rise.

events.title: Telefis Eireann begins broadcasting
events.description: National television arrives and, through programmes like the Late Late Show, becomes a solvent of deference in Irish public life.

events.title: Free secondary education
events.description: Donogh O'Malley's scheme opens secondary schooling to all, the single most consequential social reform of the century for Irish mobility.

events.title: Civil rights march in Derry
events.description: A banned civil rights march protesting discrimination in housing, jobs and voting is baton-charged by the RUC. Television footage galvanises the movement.

events.title: The Troubles begin
events.description: After sustained rioting in Derry and Belfast, British troops are deployed to Northern Ireland. Thirty years of conflict follow.

events.title: Bloody Sunday in Derry
events.description: British paratroopers shoot dead thirteen unarmed civil rights marchers in the Bogside. Recruitment to the Provisional IRA surges and Stormont is suspended.

events.title: Ireland joins the EEC
events.description: Membership ends economic dependence on Britain, opens continental markets and brings decades of structural funding.

events.title: The hunger strikes
events.description: Ten republican prisoners die at the Maze, Bobby Sands first, after being elected an MP. The deaths transform Sinn Fein into an electoral force.

events.title: Anglo-Irish Agreement
events.description: Dublin gains a consultative role in Northern Ireland for the first time, over furious unionist opposition. It sets the template for later negotiation.

events.title: Mary Robinson elected President
events.description: The first woman elected President, a liberal lawyer, becomes a symbol and a driver of a rapidly modernising society.

events.title: Homosexuality decriminalised
events.description: Following a European Court ruling won by David Norris, the state repeals the Victorian laws criminalising gay men.

events.title: IRA ceasefire
events.description: The Provisional IRA announces a complete cessation of military operations, followed by the loyalist paramilitaries, opening the way to negotiation.

events.title: Divorce legalised
events.description: A referendum removes the constitutional ban on divorce by the narrowest of margins, roughly half a per cent.

events.title: Good Friday Agreement
events.description: A settlement establishes power-sharing at Stormont, north-south and east-west institutions, and the principle of consent. Approved by referendums on both sides of the border.

events.title: Omagh bombing
events.description: A dissident republican car bomb kills 29 people, the single deadliest attack of the Troubles, and hardens support for the new agreement.

events.title: The euro replaces the pound
events.description: Euro notes and coins enter circulation, completing the monetary shift that began with the break from sterling in 1979.

events.title: IRA ends its armed campaign
events.description: The Provisional IRA formally orders an end to the armed campaign and later decommissions its weapons under independent supervision.

events.title: The bank guarantee
events.description: As the Celtic Tiger collapses, the state guarantees the liabilities of the Irish banks, transferring an enormous private debt onto the public balance sheet.

events.title: EU-IMF bailout
events.description: Ireland accepts an 85 billion euro rescue programme and years of austerity, exiting the programme in 2013.

events.title: Queen Elizabeth II visits
events.description: The first visit by a reigning British monarch since independence. She opens her Dublin Castle address in Irish and bows at the Garden of Remembrance.

events.title: Marriage equality referendum
events.description: Ireland becomes the first country in the world to legalise same-sex marriage by popular vote, carried with 62 per cent.

events.title: Repeal of the Eighth Amendment
events.description: Two-thirds vote to remove the constitutional ban on abortion, completing a decisive shift away from church authority over Irish law.

events.title: Brexit and the Northern Ireland Protocol
events.description: The UK leaves the EU, putting a customs frontier in the Irish Sea rather than on the land border and reopening constitutional argument in the north.

events.title: Sinn Fein becomes largest party in the north
events.description: For the first time a nationalist party tops the poll in a Northern Ireland Assembly election, entitling it to the office of First Minister.

events.title: Michelle O'Neill becomes First Minister
events.description: After a two-year boycott, Stormont returns and a Sinn Fein politician takes the office of First Minister for the first time in the state's history.
